claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5) · 2026-11-22T09:33Z · worktree/branch issue/3316-offset-pass-start · plan: dump each lateral rapid below Z32 in the fig8 pin run, find its source, fix on the #3316 branch if the cause is shared

Finding of the pin run, 2026-11-22. The cause of this issue is NOT shown to be shared with #3316. I release the claim.

What I did:
- Pin `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start.rs` on branch `issue/3316-offset-pass-start` (not pushed yet). Model `testdata/models/fig8.step`, tool `EM-0800-4FL`, Outside containment over the floor face.
- Heights as reported: Clearance = Top of stock +10 (Z 32), Top = Top of stock +0 (Z 22), Bottom = Selection +1.5 (Z 1.5), Stepdown 10, `retract_z: None` (hop off). Entry Helix, radius 1.6. Links are `Links::PLANAR` (Between levels "Clearance plane", Between passes "Retract plane").
- The test lists each rapid with an XY move whose lower end is below Z 32. It also reads the verifier warnings for `RapidInStock`.

What the runs show:
- Stock box margins 0, 2, 5, 10 and 20 mm around the part, and stepovers 3 and 4: zero lateral rapids below Z 32, and zero `RapidInStock` warnings. This is true for the old order (Auto) and for the new Outside order.
- The only verifier warnings are `ShankHit` on the last level (Z 1.5). The catalog tool is shorter than the 20.5 mm depth.
- Our move counts (2154 to 4488) do not agree with the reported 1764 moves. So the reported operation has a setting that the pin does not have. The candidates are the stock shape and size, the tool assembly length, and a setting on the Lead in / Lead out tab other than the defaults.

A clue from the move numbers: with 3 levels and about 588 moves for each level, moves 543, (one more) and 1711 are near the END of each level. In the Auto order the end of each level is the outermost ring work. The "cuts past the finish surface" moves 522 to 1710 have the same position in each level.

The guard test `fig8_auto_offset_keeps_every_lateral_rapid_at_the_clearance_plane` stays in the #3316 PR. It does not reproduce this issue. A second worker needs the stock and tool data of the maintainer's `2D Offset1` (not the private project file) to reproduce it.

blocked: this issue needs the stock, tool and Lead in / Lead out values of the maintainer's operation `2D Offset1` (not the private project file).

The pin run of 2026-11-22 did not show the defect with the default values (see the comment before this one). The move count of the pin (2154 to 4488) does not agree with the reported 1764 moves, so one or more settings are different.

Values that are necessary:
- Stock: the shape, the size and the offsets.
- Tool: the assembly length and the holder.
- Lead in / Lead out tab: each value that is not the default.
- Passes tab: the stepover, and each finish or spring pass setting.

The main session asks the maintainer for these values. A scout reads the code for a lateral rapid at the end of a level in the meantime.

Findings from a read of the 2D Offset planner on `origin/main`. Nothing was built or run. Each item says if it is proven by reading or a hypothesis.

- Proven by reading: with "Hop below clearance" off, each planar lateral rapid is at the clearance plane. No path that was read posts a lateral rapid below the clearance. A keep-down link that succeeds posts no rapid.
- Proven by reading: each pass link posts a vertical rapid down (`descent_dive.rs:26-30`). The verifier judges a vertical drop by its column (`crates/sim/src/verify/rapids.rs:117-124`).
- Hypothesis: the three reported moves are vertical rapids into stock, not lateral rapids. The best candidate is the restart at the pass start in `ladder_links.rs:189-199`. It runs when the entry is not Plunge. It posts a lateral rapid at the clearance and then a vertical rapid down to the material top plus 2 mm (`descent.rs:352`, `descent_dive.rs:106-168`). It occurs one time for each level, which agrees with three moves.
- The level links (Helix from the level before) occur only two times for three levels.
- 2D Offset has no finish pass and no spring pass. The settings that change the move count are the stepover, the stock to leave, the containment and its offset, the corner relief and the blend turns.

To decide this, a move dump of the reported operation is necessary: for moves 543, about 1127 and 1711, the start point and the end point (X, Y, Z). If X and Y are equal at the two ends, the move is a vertical drop, and the question is which material top the drop uses.
claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5) · 2026-11-22T16:45Z · worktree/branch issue/3319-rapids-below-clearance · plan: bounded one-setting-at-a-time search on fig8.step, red test first on a hit

Result of the bounded search, 2026-11-22. issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5).

## Method

- Headless only: `camcraft-cli mcp` (release build), no window. Model `testdata/models/fig8.step` only. No private file was opened.
- Two builds: `origin/main` 835556814, and v0.25.0 (7e2a8119c, the build of the report).
- Base: tool `EM-0800-4FL`, `fit_stock` box sides `[5,5,5,5,0,2]` (part Z 0..20, stock top Z 22), 2D Offset on the bottom face (Z 0), containment Outside, Clearance = Top of stock +10 (Z 32), Top = Top of stock +0, Bottom = Selection +1.5, Stepdown 10, stepover 4, Entry Helix r 1.6, `retract_z` null (hop off). Links are the defaults.
- One setting changed in each run. Each run: `generate`, `verify` (findings by kind and move), and `post` (Fanuc).
- The catalog tool has a 20 mm flute. The base program has `shank_hit` on the last level, so the post is blocked. Thus each case ran two times: as given, and with `flute_len` 25 ("+long"). The "+long" program posts, and a parser lists each G0 with XY motion below the highest G0 Z.

## Table

| Setting | Values | Lateral G0 below Z 32 | `rapid_in_stock` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | - | 0 | 0 |
| Entry | Plunge, Ramp, Arc | 0 | 0 (Arc, Ramp: `crossing` only) |
| Helix radius | 0.5, 3.0 (6.0 refused) | 0 | 0 |
| Level to level (`transition`) | Plunge, Ramp, Helix, Arc | 0 | 0 (Arc: 1 `crossing`) |
| Between levels | Retract, Keep down | 0 | 0 |
| Between passes | Clearance, Keep down | 0 | 0 |

| Ramp to depth, helix CW, max stay down 50, ramp angle 10 | on | 0 | 0 |
| Stock box sides | 0, 2, 10, 20 mm; asymmetric `[0,20,0,20]`; -Z 2; +Z 0, 5, 12 | 0 | 0 |
| Stock shape | cylinder, `fit_stock` margin 2 | 0 | 0 |
| Tool flute length | **10**, 25, 30 | 0 | **3 (flute 10)**, else 0 |

The v0.25.0 build gives the same results for base, flute 10, stock margin 2, stepover 3, Plunge, cylinder stock and stock sides 0.

2D Offset has no finish pass and no spring pass, so these were not swept.

## The hit: flute length 10

- Findings: `shank_hit` on moves 1406-1658 and 2194-2446, and `rapid_in_stock` on moves 1659, 2193 and 2447 (2448 moves).
- The pattern agrees with the report: three `rapid_in_stock` moves, each next to a run of part-contact moves, and the last one near the end of the program.
- The three moves are VERTICAL. Moves 1659 and 2447 are the lifts to Z 32 at (-0.202, -33.998), at the end of the outer ring of levels Z 2 and Z 1.5. Move 2193 is the rapid drop to Z 4 at the same point. Each lateral G0 is at Z 32.

## Cause

- The warning does not come from the stock rapid law (`crates/sim/src/verify/rapids.rs`). It comes from the part-solid law, `crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs:214-237`. That law judges each rapid against the PART solid and pushes `Warning::RapidInStock` when the tool meets the part.
- The outer ring of each level runs along the part wall. When the ring touches the part (here the shank, which is wider than the cutter; in the report the edge, `cuts past the finish surface`, #3323), the vertical lift out of the ring and the drop into it touch the part too. The law convicts these rapids.
- The text of `RapidInStock` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs:467-468`) says "travels through stock (below the clearance plane, or at it below the stock top)". This text is wrong for a vertical rapid that meets the part.
- Conclusion: the search found no lateral G0 below the clearance plane with the hop off. The three moves in the report are most probably the lift and drop rapids beside the gouge runs of #3323. The post is blocked, so no unsafe program is written.

## Follow-up

- #3520 (P3): the verifier text for a rapid that the part-solid law convicts.
- The gouge itself is #3323 (`P?`). This search did not reproduce that gouge on `fig8.step`.

No code change and no PR. The branch `issue/3319-rapids-below-clearance` has no commit and is deleted. The issue goes back to `blocked`. The maintainer decides if #3319 closes as a result of #3323 and #3520.

Maintainer decision, 2026-11-22, given in the question dialog.

The maintainer answered that the flute length of the tool in his operation is about 10 mm. The search of comment 7082488036 reproduces the three `RapidInStock` warnings with exactly that setting. So the cause is found:
- The three flagged moves are VERTICAL rapids at the outer-ring start, not lateral rapids below the clearance plane. With hop off, every lateral rapid stays at Z 32 (60+ runs, none below).
- The cutter is shorter than the cut depth, so the shank or holder meets the part. The part-solid check raises the rapids and also `shank_hit`. The post is blocked in that case, so no unsafe program posts.
- The text "travels through stock (below the clearance plane...)" is wrong for a vertical rapid that meets the part: #3520 (P3).

The maintainer decided: **close #3319 on this answer.** The issue as filed (a lateral G0 below the clearance plane) does not exist. The remaining work is in separate issues:
- #3520: the warning text.
- A new issue: a clear message when the cutter is shorter than the cut depth, before the first rapid (the coordinator files it, P3).
- #3323 stays with its owner decision (`P?`).

Closed as not planned, with the decision above as the reason.
Follow-up: #3525 asks for a diagnostic that names the cause (a cutter shorter than the cut depth) before the first rapid finding. #3520 corrects the text of the warning.
